# MarineEdge

> Self-hosted ship due-diligence web app for trading desks in the Black Sea, the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the UAE. Search a ship by name, former name, IMO or MMSI and get its last 12 months of AIS voyages on a map, seven rule-based red flags with their evidence (sanctions-list hits, sensitive-port calls, AIS gaps, draught changes at sea, possible ship-to-ship transfers, position jumps, identity changes), a one-sentence verdict written by fixed rules, team notes, alerts and a PDF report. It records the free aisstream.io AIS feed on its own server and buys a ship's history from Datalastic only on request.

Key facts:

- Ships are identified by IMO number; name, flag and MMSI are history on the IMO.
- Findings are deterministic and explainable: every threshold lives in `config/rules.yaml` (editable in the app), every finding carries the positions it rests on, and all wording comes from `backend/app/verdict.py`. Nothing is generated by a language model. Findings are indicators, not legal conclusions.
- Sanctions: OFAC SDN, EU and UK (FCDO) lists, downloaded daily, matched on IMO number only.
- Coverage honesty: on the free terrestrial feed, a gap where no receiver can hear is shown as Info and not counted. Draught-based findings are labelled "indicator, not proof".
- Stack: plain HTML/JS PWA (no build), MapLibre GL with self-hosted Natural Earth and OpenStreetMap maps, Python FastAPI, a pure-Python rule engine, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Playwright PDF, Docker Compose with Caddy; the server updates itself from GitHub `main` only after the full test suite passes.
- Owner operates from an iPhone only; every admin setting is inside the app.
